To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hepatitis B virus encodes a protein (HBx) to hijack the cellular DDB containing E3 ubiquitination complex to degrade the Smc5-6 complex, which inhibits transcription from extra-chromosomal DNA.
HBx hijacks the DDB1 containing ubiquitin E3 ligase to target a host restriction factor, the Smc5-6 complex, for degradation.

HBx identifies the Smc complex as a host factor that inhibits extrachromosomal transcription, and by hijacking the DDB1 containing ubiquitin ligase, HBx destroys this host restriction factor to allow productive hepatitis virus gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the replication of the hepatitis B virus.
the role of the HBx protein in the regulation of viral gene expression.
the role of HBx in hepatitis B virus transcription and replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HBx protein hijacks the cellular DDB-containing E3 ubiquitin Ligase to target the Smc complex Smc5 for degradation and thereby enhances the transcription of the viral DNA.
the Smc5 complex is a restriction factor for HBV replication and HBx protein hijacks this complex to promote HBV replication.
hepatitis B virus HBx hijacks the cellular DDB complex to target the Smc5-6 complex for degradation, which allows hepatitis B virus to transcribe its genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HBx protein identifies the SmC5/6 complex, which is a host restriction factor, as its target for destruction.
HBx hijacks the DDB1 E3 ubiquitin Ligase to target the Smc5-6 complex for degradation, which allows HBV gene expression.
HBx is a viral restriction factor inhibitor, and the Smc5-6 complex is a host restriction factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HBx hijacks a cellular E3 ligase to destroy a cellular restriction factor.
the HBx protein hijacks the DDB1 containing ubiquitin ligase, and this is the mechanism by which HBx enhances extrachromosomally transcribed viral genes.
HBx is not only a transcriptional activator, but also a suppressor of host restriction factors.
